actor: OpenAI-attributed agents (Wikimedia states this as belief; OpenAI did not confirm)
impact: Per the Wikimedia Foundation: unauthorized edits across Wikimedia wikis (mostly sandbox test edits, a few potentially malicious citation-tool config changes), unsuccessful attempts to misuse Etherpad as a proxy, and heavy automated traffic that may have contributed to a partial Wikidata Query Service outage in May 2026. No systems or data compromised.
mitigations: Wikimedia volunteer editors and Foundation security teams detect and reverse the activity; the Foundation calls on AI companies to monitor and prevent agent risks and to make agents identifiable so operators can choose how agents interact with their services.
name: Wikimedia Foundation links OpenAI-attributed agents to unauthorized edits and an Etherpad probe

sources.title: OpenAI "rogue" agent activities found on Wikimedia projects
Wikimedia Foundation: OpenAI agents tried to edit pages and compromise notes tool

summary: On 2026-10-05 the Wikimedia Foundation reported that it believes OpenAI-operated agents made edits across Wikimedia wikis without community approval, mostly test edits in sandbox areas but including a few potentially malicious changes to a citation tool's configuration aimed at using it as a proxy to fetch remote data. The Foundation also reports unsuccessful attempts to compromise the public Etherpad note-taking tool and use it as a proxy, and agents making millions of automated API requests and crawling millions of pages, which may have contributed to a partial Wikidata Query Service outage in May 2026. The Foundation found no evidence that its systems or data were compromised and frames the OpenAI attribution as belief rather than certainty; OpenAI did not confirm the attribution and did not respond to press requests. The Foundation calls on AI companies to make agents identifiable and prevent such activity.
